sections.h2: Where is South Portland, Maine, and what is it like?
sections.html:
South Portland is a Cumberland County city on Portland Harbor, directly across the water from Portland's skyline. It covers about 14 square miles, of which roughly 12 are land. Portland borders it to the north, Cape Elizabeth and Scarborough to the south, and Westbrook to the west.

The city is a collection of small named areas rather than one center. They include Ferry Village, the oldest, along with Cushing's Point, Knightville, Mill Creek, Ligonia, Pleasantdale, Brick Hill, Redbank, Cash Corner, Thornton Heights, Meetinghouse Hill and Willard Beach. The Maine Mall district is also a distinct part of the city.

The Census Bureau estimates 27,007 residents as of July 1, 2025. Parks and trails add to the appeal for buyers, including Willard Beach, a three-mile paved Greenbelt with harbor views and 40-acre Hinckley Park.

sections.h2: How did South Portland become its own city?
sections.html:
South Portland split from Cape Elizabeth in 1895 after a dispute over future drinking water. It was incorporated as a town on March 15, 1895, and became a city in 1898. Like Portland, it draws its water from Sebago Lake.

Shipbuilding then changed the housing map. Todd-Bath Iron Shipbuilding was founded in 1940 to build ships for Britain, and together with the West Yard the shipyards built 236 Liberty ships, employing about 30,000 people at the peak. That workforce needed homes quickly, which is one reason many neighborhoods contain compact houses from the mid twentieth century. Fort Preble, established in 1808, and Spring Point Ledge Light, built in 1897, are older landmarks.

  • Ferry Village and Cushing's Point hold the oldest housing.
  • Knightville and Mill Creek developed around commerce and the harbor.
  • Willard Beach and Thornton Heights are older residential neighborhoods with their own buyer followings.

sections.h2: What drives the South Portland economy and commute?
sections.html:
South Portland is known as Maine's retail center and also has a working waterfront. The Maine Mall is the state's largest mall, and Mill Creek's strip mall, built in the 1950s, was the first of its kind in Maine. The Portland-Montreal Pipe Line delivers oil to a terminal with more than 120 tanks, and Rigby Yard, built in 1922, is New England's largest railroad yard.

Semiconductor manufacturing is also present, with plants run by Diodes Incorporated and Texas Instruments.

Getting around is straightforward. The Casco Bay Bridge links the city to Portland, I-95 runs through it, and the city-owned South Portland Bus Service provides local transit. The main runway of the Portland International Jetport lies inside South Portland's limits, although the passenger terminal is in Portland. Homes under flight paths can draw questions from buyers about noise, so be ready with an honest answer.

sections.h2: How do schools factor into a South Portland sale?
sections.html:
South Portland runs its own school system, and that is a draw for families. The public schools are Brown, Dyer, Kaler, Skillin and Dora L. Small elementary schools, South Portland Middle School for grades 5 to 8, and South Portland High School. Private options include Holy Cross School and Greater Portland Christian School.

Southern Maine Community College is also in the city. If your house falls near a school or campus, mention it in any listing, but do not promise enrollment boundaries, which the school department sets.

sections.h2: How is property tax billed in South Portland?
sections.html:
South Portland sends one annual tax mailing with two payment stubs, due in May and November. The city moved away from quarterly bills. The City Council sets the exact rate and due dates each year in the budget orders, so confirm them on the Finance Department page.

The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value, up 3.4 percent from $13.20, and about 30 percent below the 2019 rate of $19.70. The tax commitment date was September 11, 2025, and assessments are set as of April 1. The city reports a 100 percent certified ratio against a state minimum of 91 percent.

sections.h2: What happens if South Portland property taxes are behind?
sections.html:
Unpaid South Portland tax follows Maine's lien timeline, and a sale can clear it. Under 36 M.R.S. section 942, the tax collector sends a 30-day demand notice between 8 months and one year after commitment, then records a lien certificate. Under section 943, the lien mortgage is deemed foreclosed if unpaid 18 months after filing.

  • The city notes that owners with taxes in lien should contact General Assistance at 207-767-7617 about a hardship abatement.
  • The City Council can consider hardship abatements for owners who cannot afford their taxes.
  • An error or illegality application must be filed within 185 days of commitment under 36 M.R.S. section 841.

The tax bill is paid from closing proceeds if you sell. A written proration agreement with the buyer can also let the treasurer record a certificate that you paid your share.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and closing costs apply in South Portland?
sections.html:
Maine's transfer tax is $2.20 per $500 of value, split evenly between buyer and seller. For a $600,000 sale, the total would be $2,640, or $1,320 each, as an example only. Transfers on or after November 1, 2025 also pay an extra $3.80 per $500 above $1 million.

The deed is recorded at the Cumberland County registry, and recording costs $40 for most submitters. Any exemption has to be stated on the declaration of value form. Maine Revenue Services publishes the transfer tax rules.

sections.h2: What rental rules apply to South Portland owners?
sections.html:
Owners of buildings with three or more dwelling units or rooming units must register them with the city. That requirement comes from Chapter 5, Article VII of the South Portland Code of Ordinances, effective January 1, 2012. Short-term rentals must also be registered with the city, and the registration is renewed each year through the City Clerk's office.

If you are selling a rental, tell buyers early whether it is registered. A cash buyer can take over the building with tenants in place.

sections.h2: How can I sell a South Portland house fast?
sections.html:
A cash sale is quickest, and a listing may net more for a house in good shape. South Portland attracts a lot of buyers because of its location next to Portland, so a clean, updated house can sell on the open market. A house that needs a roof, a heating system or probate work often does better with a direct buyer.

  • Ask us for a written offer and compare it with a listing net after commission and repairs.
  • Bring the deed, mortgage statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Check the Finance Department for any unpaid balance before closing.

We buy as-is, with no commission or closing fees charged to you.

faqs.q: What is the South Portland mil rate?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 mil rate is $13.65 per $1,000 of assessed value, according to the city's December 2025 assessing presentation. One slide in that document shows 13.64.

faqs.q: When are South Portland property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due twice a year, in May and November, with one annual mailing that includes two stubs. The City Council sets the exact dates each year, so check the Finance Department page.

faqs.q: Does South Portland have a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The Maine homestead exemption reduces taxable value by $25,000, which the city says is worth $341.25 in tax at the current rate. It applies to your permanent residence.

faqs.q: Can I sell a South Portland house that is in a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien payoff comes from your proceeds at closing. A lien that is not redeemed within 18 months of filing is deemed foreclosed under Maine law, so earlier action protects your equity.

faqs.q: Who pays the Maine transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer and seller split it equally at $2.20 per $500 of value. An extra $3.80 per $500 applies to the part above $1 million for transfers after November 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Do South Portland short-term rentals need registration?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires short-term rentals to be registered, and renewal is annual. Buildings with three or more units must also be registered under the rental ordinance.
